title: Centor criteria
subtitle: Alternative acute sore-throat score
summary: Centor estimates likelihood of group A streptococcal infection and is not an airway or sepsis rule-out tool.
population: People with acute pharyngitis or tonsillitis undergoing clinical assessment; the original score was derived in adults.
exclusions: Use the appropriate paediatric pathway for children; assess children under 5 with fever using NICE guidance on fever in under 5s.
Do not delay emergency assessment for airway compromise, severe systemic illness or suppurative complications.

criteria.label: Tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy
criteria.description: Painful/tender nodes at the front of the neck.

results.label: Do not offer antibiotics for uncomplicated acute sore throat
interpretation: At Centor 0�2, antibiotics are not routinely indicated for uncomplicated acute sore throat.
actions: Advise fluids and suitable analgesia; explain that symptoms commonly last about 1 week
Advise prompt medical help for rapid or significant worsening or systemic illness, or if improvement has not begun after 1 week

results.label: More likely to benefit
interpretation: The patient is more likely to benefit from an immediate or back-up antibiotic, depending on clinical findings and local guidance.
actions: Consider an immediate or back-up antibiotic after clinical assessment; if treatment is indicated, phenoxymethylpenicillin is first line, with alternatives guided by allergy, pregnancy and current local policy
If a back-up prescription is issued, advise use if improvement has not started within 3 to 5 days or symptoms worsen rapidly or significantly
Advise prompt medical help for marked worsening or systemic illness

overrides: Escalate immediately for suspected airway compromise. Refer to hospital for severe systemic infection or a severe suppurative complication such as quinsy, deep-neck abscess or Lemierre syndrome.

People who are systemically very unwell, have signs of a more serious condition or are at high risk of complications need an immediate antibiotic decision under the relevant pathway regardless of score.
limitations: Do not use as a standalone prescribing or disposition instruction.
